Text:
# CHOLANGITIS

[Oral step-down treatment](step-down-treatment)

Most cases are due to common bile duct obstruction. Obstruction (if present) must be relieved with an endoscopical, transcutaneous, or surgical procedure. The most common pathogens isolated are E. coli, Klebsiella, Enterococcus and Enterobacter. Anaerobic coverage is recommended. Antimicrobials' role in cholangitis is to allow patients to have elective and not emergently scheduled drainage procedures. Due to increasing resistance, fluoroquinolones are only recommended in cases of severe penicillin and cephalosporin allergy.

---

References:

- Mandell chapter: Infections of the Liver and Biliary System (Liver Abscess, Cholangitis, Cholecystitis)
- Sanford Guide article: Gallbladder Infections
- Solomkin et al, Clin Infect Dis, 2010, 50:133-64
- Up-to-Date article: Acute cholangitis
Therapy:
## Inpatient

### Treatment of patients on ward without systemic symptoms of infection

Treat for 4-7 days after source control.

Preferred:
Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h [M] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI]
< OR >
Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h [M] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg PO q8h [DI]

### Treatment of patients in ICU with systemic symptoms of infection

Treat for 4-7 days after source control.

Preferred:
Piperacillin-Tazobactam 4.5 g IV q8h extended infusion [R]
Alternative for beta lactam allergy (No angioedema, anaphylaxis or urticaria)
Cefepime 2 gm IV q8h [R] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI]

< OR >
Cefepime 2 gm IV q8h [R] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg PO q8h [DI]
Alternative for severe beta-lactam allergy (ie. Anaphylaxis, urticaria)
Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction
Meropenem 500 mg IV q6h [R,O]

## ER/UC

### Treatment of patients on ward without systemic symptoms of infection

Treat for 4-7 days after source control.

Preferred:
Ceftriaxone 2 gm once STAT [M]

Biliary structural abnormality, including stent:
<ADD> Metronidazole 500 mg IV once STAT [DI] to above regimen

### Treatment of patients in ICU with systemic symptoms of infection

Treat for 4-7 days after source control.

Preferred:
Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV once STAT [R]

Alternative:
Cefepime 2 gm IV once STAT [R] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV once STAT [DI]

Alternative for severe beta-lactam reaction:
Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction
Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV once STAT [R,DI] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV once STAT [DI]
